sentences.text:
THE FILE OF THE XI ADDITIONAL DISTRICT JUDGE AND ADDITIONAL MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL, BELAGAVI, AWARDING COMPENSATION OF Rs.4,78,000/- WITH INTEREST AT 6%
P.A. FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL ITS PAYMENT.

THIS APPEAL IS COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  MFA No. 103071 of 2019  JUDGMENT
Challenging impugned judgment and award dated 08.03.2019, passed by XI Additional District Judge and Additional M.A.C.T., Belagavi, in MVC No.2799/2017, this appeal is filed.

2. Brief facts as stated are that on 26.11.2017, when Kumar Prathviraj S/o Narashing Kadam, was about to cross road near Darshini Hotel, Chikkodi, driver of NWKRTC bus bearing registration no.KA- 22/F-1610 driven bus in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to him, causing accident.
In said accident, he sustained sever injuries.
Despite of taking treatment in several hospitals, he did not recover fully and sustained permanent disability.
Claiming compensation, he filed claim petition against NWKRTC under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act.
3. On service of notice, respondent entered appearance and filed objections denying entire claim petition averments.
It was specifically contended that bus was not involved in any accident on said day and claim petition was false and also excessive.

4. Based on pleadings, tribunal framed followings issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 26.11.2017 at about 03-15 p.m. near Bus stand at chikkodi town on Belagavi-chikkodi road, petitioner sustained injuries due to the rash or negligent driving of Bus bearing No.KA- 42/F-1610?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, at what amount and from whom?
3. What order or award?
5. Thereafter, it recorded evidence of claimant mother as PW.1 and Dr.S.R.Angadi as P.W.2 and Ex.P.1 to P.13 were marked.
In rebuttal driver of bus was examined as R.W.1 and Ex.R.1 to 6 were marked.

entities.text: Divisional Controller, Nwkrtc vs Kumar Prathviraj
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On consideration, tribunal answered issue no.1 in affirmative, issue no.2 partly in affirmative and issue no.3 by holding NWKRTC liable to pay compensation of Rs.4,78,000/- with interest at rate of 6% per annum.
Challenging same NWKRTC is in appeal.
7. Sri
. S.C.Bhuti, learned counsel for NWKRTC submitted that on 26.11.2017 when bus came from bus stand towards Basava Circle, Bolero jeep dashed against claimant and sped away without stopping.
However, on 27.11.2017 at 7.00 p.m., complaint was lodged against driver of bus for causing accident.
On 29.11.2017, bus was seized i.e. four days after accident.
Though, claimant alleged rash and negligent driving of bus, they did not lead any evidence to substantiate same.

Relying merely upon Police investigation records and ignoring deposition of bus driver as R.W.1,
who stated that accident was caused by driver of Bolero jeep, tribunal held negligence against bus driver.
8. Even on quantum it was further submitted that tribunal committed grave error.
During cross examination, claimant admitted that doctor who treated claimant was available within 1 k.m., of tribunal.
But they had examined doctor-R.S.Angadi, who had not treated claimant but made grossly excessive assessment of disability.

Taking same into account, tribunal awarded compensation under second slab in Master Mallikarjun v/s Divisional Manager, The National Insurance Co. Ltd., and Anr., reported in AIR 2014 SC 736, in stead of first slab.

entities.text: Master Mallikarjun v/s Divisional Manager, The National Insurance Co. Ltd., and Anr., reported in AIR 2014 SC 736
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was further submitted that award under other heads was also not sustainable.
9. On other hand, Smt.Geetha K.M., learned counsel for respondent/claimant supported award and sought dismissal of appeal.
It was submitted that on appreciation of entire evidence tribunal had passed impugned award and there was no merit in any of contention.

10. Heard learned counsel, perused judgment and award and records.
11.
From above submission, occurrence of accident on 26.11.2017 and claimant sustaining injuries in said accident are not in dispute.
NWKRTC is in appeal alleging false implication of NWKRTC Bus and also on quantum.
Claimant has not filed appeal.

12. From above submissions, only point that arises for consideration is:
"1.
Whether finding of tribunal regarding involvement of NWKRTC Bus calls for interference?

2. Whether assessment of compensation by tribunal calls for modification as sought for?"
13. Point no.1: Insofar as false implication of vehicle, from deposition of PW-1, it is seen that on said date, on receipt of information about claimant having sustained injuries in accident, P.W.1 rushed to spot and thereafter took claimant to hospital for treatment.
she is not eyewitness.
Since hospital at Chikkodi referred claimant for higher treatment, he was shifted to hospital in Belgavi.

Thereafter,
complaint is filed.

In view of above since claimant had sustained severe injuries initially referred to The Divisional Controller, Nwkrtc vs Kumar Prathviraj S/O Narashing Kadam on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156259167/
3 hospital at Chikkodi and thereafter hospital at Belagavi, delay of one day in filing complaint would not be fatal.

entities.text: Divisional Controller, Nwkrtc vs Kumar Prathviraj S/O Narashing Kadam
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In wound certificate issued by Government hospital at Chikodi, history of injury is noted as due to road traffic accident.

Even in wound certificate issued by KLE hospital at Belagavi,
history of injuries is stated to be due to hit and run by vehicle.
Though, they may give scope for some suspicion, same would not clearly established that either bus was not involved or that alleged Bolero vehicle itself caused accident.
14. While passing impugned award, tribunal has examined deposition of RW-1 - driver also.

However, suggestion by claimant that only for purposes of avoiding liability of NWKRTC, RW-1 was deposing falsely was denied.
15.
Relying upon result of police investigation report, claimants have filed claim petition.
For purposes claiming compensation, said prima facie evidence would be sufficient, burden would be on respondent denying accident to establish same.

By mere examination of driver and denying involvement of vehicle, said purpose would not be achieved Examination of any of passenger or investigating officer or such other evidence was perhaps required.
In absence, view taken by tribunal cannot be dispelled.
Hence, point no.1 is answered in negative.
16. Point no.2: Insofar as quantum of compensation, claimant was 10 year old boy studying in 5th Standard.

He sustained injuries as follows:
1. Head injury with mucosal thickening in bilateral maxillary sinuses.
2. Left lower limb extensive subfacial degloving wound with tibia fracture.
3. Right thigh degloving wound.
17.
For said injuries, claimant was treated initially at General Hospital, Chikkodi, thereafter at KLE Hospital, Belagavi and lastly at Vijaya Ortho and Trauma Centre, Belagavi for a period of 21 days.

entities.text: Vijaya Ortho and Trauma Centre, Belagavi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: From Ex.P8, it is seen that claimant sustained degloving injuries on both legs.
From Ex.P9 - X-ray report, malunited fracture of 1/3rd shaft of left tibia is seen.

PW-2 has issued Ex.P10 - Disability certificate, wherein he as noted that there is restriction of flexion of right knee and based on same,
he assessed limb disability at 35%.

Tribunal, considered whole body disability at 16% and by applying ratio in Master Mallikarjun v/s Divisional Manager, The National Insurance Co. Ltd., and Anr., reported in AIR 2014 SC 736, awarded compensation of Rs.3,00,000/-.

entities.text: Master Mallikarjun v/s Divisional Manager, The National Insurance Co. Ltd., and Anr., reported in AIR 2014 SC 736
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per said decision, it also awarded compensation of Rs.1,37,000/- against medical bills.
18. Apart from same, it has awarded Rs.20,000/- towards discomfort, inconvenience and loss of earnings of parents and Rs.21,000/- towards diet, attendants and nutrition etc.

Though,
nomenclature of said compensation may not fit be in tune with MASTER MALLIKARJUN'S case (supra), accident has occurred in year 2017, notional income for said period is Rs.10,250/-.

If a period of three months is taken as lay off, compensation towards loss of income of parents for said period would be Rs.30,750/- therefore, award of Rs.41,000/- under other heads apart from medical bills cannot be said to be grossly excessive or unjustified.
Thus, point no.2 is answered in negative.
